purpose: One-fetch onboarding for machine buyers: everything an autonomous agent needs to go from discovery to a settled paid call on any RAEN x402 wall - route, live-verified price, ready-to-send request body, settlement asset, and trust verification. Companion to registry/payto-registry.json (payTo verification, case rules, poison-address rejection).
verified_method: Every price below was confirmed by sending an UNPAID request to the live paid route on 2026-11-22 and re-verified 2026-11-23, capturing the HTTP 402 payment-required header, base64-decoding it, and reading accepts[].amount. Request bodies are taken from the service's own /.well-known/x402.json advertisement. Live challenge > manifest > this file: if they ever disagree, trust the live 402 and re-fetch this bundle.

settlement.mechanism: EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization; on 402, sign the exact challenge terms, attach the signed payment to a retry of the same request, receive the payload on 2xx.
settlement.first_call_free_note: royal-ruby and raen-mcp-gateway support free first calls (charge-and-rebate / dev key) - see service notes.

how_to_first_call: 1. Pick a service below; send the unpaid request with its example_body.
2. Expect HTTP 402 with a payment-required header (that is the receipt of a healthy wall, not an error).
3. base64-decode the header; verify accepts[].payTo == canonical_payto (case-insensitive) and accepts[].amount matches this bundle. Reject retired 0x7861...1393 and any lookalike.
4. Pay: build an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization for the USDC amount on Base, sign with your wallet, attach per the challenge's x402 fields, retry the request.
5. Verify: on 2xx read the payload; the settlement appears as a USDC Transfer event to canonical_payto on Base (e.g. via eth_getLogs or Basescan).

trust_verification.rule: Verify the live 402 challenge payTo against canonical_payto case-insensitively before paying. Manifests and directories (including Lumi/Bazaar caches) can carry stale or poisoned addresses; the live challenge is the source of truth.

self_verify.purpose: Before paying, verify the wall yourself in one command - no directory, registry, or cache trusted.
self_verify.command: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST <route-url> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw '<example_body JSON>' | grep -i payment-required | cut -d' ' -f2- | python -c "import sys,base64,json;a=json.loads(base64.b64decode(sys.stdin.read().strip()+'=='))['accepts'][0];print(a['scheme'],a['network'],a['payTo'],a['amount'])"
self_verify.pass_criteria: scheme=exact, network=eip155:8453, payTo=0x9b8a27e03ceba490953cda8ab1291c0e13baf72f (case-insensitive), amount matches the service price below.
self_verify.note: All 6 challenges (5 POST + royal-ruby GET) were re-decoded with this exact recipe on 2026-11-22 and passed.

claims_desk.purpose: Paid but got nothing? Do not pay again. Every RAEN payment is tracked on-chain, including transfers to the retired payee (stranding watch).
claims_desk.lookup_your_payment: GET https://settlement-collector.fly.dev/storefront/claims?tx=<your tx hash>  OR  ?payer=<your wallet address>
claims_desk.claim_code_rule: RAEN-<sha256(tx)[:10]> uppercase — derivable from your own tx hash; the lookup confirms it and its state (open | delivered | credit_redeemed | recorded).
claims_desk.register_for_redelivery: POST https://settlement-collector.fly.dev/storefront/register {tx_or_intent: <tx or payer>, email: <you>} or {tx_or_intent, agent_id, callback_url} for machine webhook delivery; a new registration target re-arms re-delivery.
claims_desk.prepaid_credit_verify: GET https://settlement-collector.fly.dev/storefront/credits/<claim code> (redeem: POST .../credits/<code>/redeem) — one-time; services accept it as X-RAEN-CREDIT instead of a new payment.
claims_desk.retired_payee_watch: GET https://settlement-collector.fly.dev/storefront/legacy-watch — USDC transfers to retired 0x7861db4efc14a1ed5dd8c96c528a3796560f1393 auto-create an order + claim code; the same tx/payer lookup finds them.

first_settled_call.purpose: Zero to a settled paid call in one request. The cheapest settled liveness probe we know of in the x402 ecosystem (prove us wrong).
steps: 1. curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://royal-ruby-x402.fly.dev/api/ping -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' -w '%{http_code}' -> expect 402 + payment-required header.
2. base64-decode the header; verify accepts[].amount == 1000 ($0.001) and payTo == canonical_payto.
3. Pay per the settlement mechanism and retry with the payment attached. Expect 2xx JSON: {status:'alive', block, latency_ms, catalog...}.
4. Verify settlement: USDC Transfer of 1000 atomic units to canonical_payto on Base.

proven_end_to_end.result: settled 0.001 USDC on Base (Transfer to canonical payTo, block 61054191), payload returned same-response; full round trip 1067ms
